The meeting was called to order by Chair Lopez at 6:00 p.m., in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were
Commissioner Macias, Vice Chair Apodaca, and Chair Lopez. Commissioner Barragan
and Commissioner Vernola-Salas were absent. Also present were Alex Hamilton, Interim
Director of Community Development; Nancy Lee, Development Services Manager; Anita
Lakhani, Deputy City Attorney, (participated remotely); Carlos Rojas, Senior Planner;
Kristy Wong, Associate Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Planning Commission
Meeting of November 12, 2025.

WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS PERMIT (WTP) NO. 2025-05
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST (DAR) NO. 2025-16
John McDonald of Eukon Group, for AT&T (“Applicant”); a request to construct and
operate an unmanned wireless telecommunications facility designed as a freestanding
60-foot faux mono-elm tree; and a request to install an eight (8) foot high wrought iron
fence to enclose the 165 square foot ancillary equipment area. The subject site is 1.17
acres in size and is generally known as 11205 Imperial Highway (also known as
Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8022-035-023), located within the C-3 (General
Commercial) Zone. Environmental: Consider and find that the proposed project is exempt
from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to Section 15303 (New
Construction of Small Structures).

Chair Lopez opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Senior Planner Rojas presented
a report stating that the applicant’s requests are: (1) to construct and operate an
unmanned wireless telecommunications facility designed as a freestanding 60-foot-high
faux mono-elm tree; and (2) to install an eight-foot-high wrought iron fence ancillary
equipment enclosure to deviate from maximum allowable height requirements.

Further, he indicted that the proposed enclosure will be located approximately 168-feet
away from the nearest residential property line and 180-feet away from the nearest
residential dwelling unit; that the proposal will also involve the placement of a 165-square
foot equipment enclosure which will house both the wireless facility, as well as the
equipment cabinets; and that the proposed enclosure will be 16 feet by 10 feet.

Continuing with his presentation, Mr. Rojas shared that the proposed project complies
with both the General Plan and Zoning Code as well as the applicable development
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  December 10, 2025

standards for wireless telecommunications facilities, and is exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); therefore, staff recommends that the Planning
Commission approve the applications subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in
Resolution Nos. 25-23 and 25-24.

John McDonald, representing AT&T, stated that he is here to answer any questions that
the Commission may have related to the site.

In response to Vice Chair Apodaca’s comment if there is any discernable sound
generated by the equipment, Mr. McDonald replied that there is a very low sound coming
from the cabinets that will not be noticeable by anyone walking on the sidewalk; and that
the sound can only be heard by someone being within five to ten feet of the enclosure.

Vice Chair Apodaca commented on the appearance of these faux trees, and she asked
how long do they remain in good condition. Mr. McDonald stated that the old ones lasted
about ten to fifteen years, but that the new ones last about thirty years; and that if any
issues arise, they will be replacing the branches.

In reply to Commissioner Macias’ comment on how often would they be servicing the site,
Mr. McDonald indicated that, typically, they would service the site if there is a power
outage or once every year or every two years.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Lopez closed the
public hearing.

It was moved by Vice Chair Apodaca and seconded by Chair Lopez to: (1) Adopt
Resolution No. 25-23 to approve Wireless Telecommunications Permit No. 2025-05
subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; (2) Adopt Resolution No.
25-24 to approve Director Approval Request No. 2025-16 subject to the Conditions of
Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and (3) Consider and find that the proposed project is
exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15303 (New Construction of Small Structures).

WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS PERMIT (WTP) NO. 2024-02
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST (DAR) NO. 2025-09
Leticia Smith of Smartlink, on behalf of APC Towers (“Applicant”); a request to construct
and operate an unmanned wireless telecommunications facility designed as a 60-foot
mono-pine and install an eight (8) foot high block wall to enclose the equipment area.
The subject property, at one (1) acre in size, is generally known as 12616 Pioneer
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 3

Boulevard (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (APN) 8048-013-011), located
within the C-3 (General Commercial) zone.

Chair Lopez opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Associate Planner Wong
presented a report stating that the applicant’s requests are: (1) to construct and operate
an unmanned wireless telecommunications facility designed as a 60-foot-high mono-pine
tree; and (2) to allow an eight-foot-high block wall to enclose the equipment area to
deviate from maximum allowable height requirements.

Further, Ms. Wong indicated that the proposed wireless facility will consist of a 34 foot by
40 foot area enclosed with an eight-foot high concrete masonry unit (CMU) wall and a 12-
foot-long double wide swing access gate; that the proposed mono-pine will be located
approximately 15 feet and 5 inches from the nearest residential property line and 21 feet
and 3 inches from the nearest residential dwelling unit; and that the mono-pine tower has
an overall height of 60 feet, consisting of a 55-foot mono-pine and a 5-foot high lightning
rod.

Continuing with her presentation, Ms. Wong shared that on October 30, 2025, the
applicant hosted a community outreach meeting due to the subject site’s proximity to
residential properties; that one property owner who attended the meeting voiced a
concern regarding the proximity of the facility to said property owner’s dwelling and noise
generated during routine maintenance; that according to the applicant, the generator is in
line with current ambient noise levels and will not affect current conditions; that the
proposed development is consistent with the General Plan and will support community
growth and change through the provision and maintenance of quality public services and
facilities through improved phone services in the area; that the project complies with the
zoning code with the approval of Director Approval Request No. 2025-09 and the General
Plan, as well as being exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act; therefore,
staff recommends that the Commission approve the applicant’s request subject to the
Conditions of Approval contained in Resolution Nos. 25-25 and 25-26.

Veronica Arvizu of Smartlink, on behalf of Verizon, presented testimony stating that
Condition of Approval Nos. 22 and 23 pertain to the backup generator and addresses
noise; that Condition of Approval Nos. 19 and 49 both deal with graffiti removal; that there
is a discrepancy in that Condition No. 19 requires graffiti removal within twenty-four hours
of notification and Condition No. 49 requires graffiti removal within forty-eight hours; that
they would ask if it is possible to allow graffiti removal within seventy-two hours; and that
all of the other conditions look good.

In response to Vice Chair Apodaca’s request for clarification on the maintenance of the
generator, Ms. Arvizu indicated that maintenance would occur during power outages or
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 4
Minutes of the Special Meeting  December 10, 2025

emergencies, and perhaps once a month during regular business hours; that they could
add a condition to that effect from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; that according to the noise
study, the peak time for ambient noise is 3:00 p.m. in that area, and that they could
perform maintenance at that time.

Vice Chair Apodaca indicated that she would recommend graffiti removal within forty-
eight hours.

Chris Bazen stated that he and his wife live adjacent to the proposed facility at 11827
Lyndora Street; that the proposed location of the mono-pine is going to block the
afternoon sun from their recently installed roof solar system; that, currently, there is a big
Sycamore tree at the proposed site, and he asked if this tree is going to be removed.

Interim Director Hamilton indicated that there are no plans for this tree to be removed.

Theresa Bazen shared that their front entrance is probably six feet from the proposed
wall; that the area also contains a trash enclosure; that they have been having problems
with vagrants and homeless people living in that area; that fires have been set; that the
Sycamore tree is probably five feet from their front bedroom property line; that, as stated
by her husband, they just had a solar system installed; and she asked if it is possible to
have the mono-pine tree moved to the corner where the Denny’s sign is located.

The applicant’s representative, Ms. Arvizu, stated that, generally, they place the mono-
pines in the corner of properties for law enforcement visibility; that they have maintenance
crews monitoring the sites; that they have a lease in place with Denny’s ownership; and
that they would have to check with them for their preferred location.

Vice Chair Apodaca thanked the Bazens for their input and concerns. She shared that
the Commission is recommending that the public hearing of Wireless
Telecommunications Permit No. 2024-02 and Director Approval Request No. 2025-09 be
continued to the meeting of January 14, 2026, to allow time for staff to work with the
applicant to address the issues brought up, and that Condition Nos. 19 and 49 provide
that graffiti be removed within forty-eight hours of discovery. There being no objections,
it was so ordered.

the New Year.

Authority:

Section 17.02.295 (“Wireless Telecommunications Permit”) of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”)
states that the Reviewing Authority may impose such conditions as it determines are necessary and
reasonable to protect the best interests of the surrounding property or neighborhood and to ensure
compliance with the general purpose and intent of this title and the General Plan.
Section 17.02.295.C.1 of the NMC authorizes the Director of Community Development of the City
of Norwalk (“Director”) to administratively review and approve an application for a wireless
telecommunication facility permit if the facility complies with Article IV of Chapter 17.04 and as
proposed is architecturally integrated with the existing development so as to be screened,
camouflaged and visually nonobtrusive. Notwithstanding, the Director may at his or her discretion
 Norwalk Planning Commission  January 14, 2026

refer the wireless telecommunications facility permit to the Planning Commission of the City of
Norwalk (“Planning Commission”) for review.
Section 17.02.295.C.2 of the NMC requires the Planning Commission to review applications not
otherwise reviewed by the Director, including, but not limited to, applications in the public right-of-
way or located in a residential zone.
Section 17.02.203 (“Director Approval Request”) of the NMC requires the filing of a Director
Approval Request (DAR) to approve a solid wall, fence, or hedge in excess of six (6) feet in height
located elsewhere from the front setback on a lot or parcel where the Director determines that such
fence or wall will not adversely affect the public health, safety, or general welfare.
Section 17.02.203.B of the NMC authorizes the Director at his or her discretion to refer any DAR
request to the Planning Commission for review and determination.
Introduction/background:

On December 10, 2025, the Planning Commission considered Wireless Telecommunications Permit
No. 2024-02 and Director Approval Request No. 2025-09. During the public hearing, the Planning
Commission received a public comment on the structure’s shade impact on a neighboring property’s
existing solar panels. As a result, the Planning Commission voted to continue the item to the
January 14, 2026 Planning Commission Meeting so that the applicant can work on analysis of the
potential impacts to the neighbor’s solar panels.
In response, the Applicant has provided a solar report (see Attachment H) that concludes the solar
panels will receive full sunlight during peak production hours and that the neighbor’s solar panels
are located out of any shadowing possibilities as a result of the construction of the proposed mono-
pine.
The following staff report and attachments are carried over from the Planning Commissiong Meeting
on December 10, 2025.
The subject site is located at 12616 Pioneer Boulevard (APN: 8048-013-011). The subject site, at
one (1)-acre in size, has a General Plan land use designation of General Commercial and zoning
classification of C-3 (General Commercial). The subject site is situated at the southeast corner of
Imperial Highway and Pioneer Boulevard.
Per the Los Angeles County Assessor’s records, the subject site is currently developed with a 5,531
square foot commercial structure constructed in 1978. City records reflect that the structure is
operated as a restaurant (Denny’s Restaurant).
The subject property is located within a fully developed area. The property is surrounded by a Single-
Family Residential (R-1) zone to the east and General Commercial (C-3) zone to the north, south,
and west.

Project Description:

Leticia Smith of Smartlink, on behalf of APC Towers, (“Applicant”) is requesting approval of Wireless
Telecommunications Permit (WTP) No. 2024-02 to construct and operate an unmanned wireless
telecommunications facility designed as a 60-foot mono-pine and approval of Director Approval
Request (DAR) No. 2025-09 to allow an eight (8) foot high concrete masonry unit (CMU) wall to
enclose the equipment area to deviate from height requirements (“Proposed Project”).
Site Plan
The proposed project area is 34 feet by 40 feet at the southeast corner of the property. An eight (8)
foot high CMU wall is proposed to enclose the wireless telecommunications facility and the
equipment cabinets. The proposed mono-pine for the new wireless facility will be located
approximately 15 feet and five (5) inches from the nearest residential property line and 21 feet and
three (3) inches from the nearest residential dwelling unit.
Elevations
The proposed wireless facility will be equipped with the following equipment and be contained within
the proposed enclosure:
Tower Scope of Work:
  •  55’-0” Tall Mono-Pine with 5’-0” Tall Lightning Rod
  •  (12) Panel Antennas
  •  (6) Remote Radio Units (RRU)
  •  (3) Over Voltage Protections (OVP)
  •  (3) Hybrid Cables
  •  (1) Microwave (MW) Dish with (2) Outdoor Units (ODU)
Ground Scope of Work:
  •  34’-0” by 40’-0” Compound with an 8’-0” CMU Wall
  •  (3) Cabinets on Concrete Pad
  •  (1) GPS Antenna, (1) ILC, (1) Telco Box, and (1) Tech Light
  •  30-kilowatt (kW) Diesel Generator with 168 Gallon Tank on Concrete Pad
The mono-pine tower has an overall height of 60 feet, consisting of a 55-foot-high mono-pine and
five (5) foot high lighting rod. The proposed height is consistent with the height restrictions which
limit a wireless telecommunications facility to 60 feet in height within a non-residential zone per NMC
Section 17.04.300.G. The installation has been designed to minimize visual impact. A minimum of
three (3) branches per lineal foot will be installed on the mono-pine wireless tower to disguise the
antennas behind faux branches and foliage. The antennas, mounting arms, and microwave dish
along the brackets will also be painted to match the matte color of the tree foliage and soften the
industrial look. It is staff’s assessment that a mono-pine design at 60 feet in height is appropriate for
the subject site as it would allow additional opportunities for co-location.

Fences and Walls
The proposed wireless facility will consist of 34 feet by 40 feet area enclosed with an eight (8) foot
high CMU wall and 12-foot-long double wide swing access gate. The CMU equipment enclosure is
proposed to have decorative block or a stucco finish and a decorative cap paint to match the existing
structure on site. Ficus vines are proposed as landscaping on the exterior walls of the enclosure to
deter graffiti and loitering.
Off-Street Parking
The subject site has 63 existing parking spaces. The Proposed Project will result in the loss of two
(2) parking spaces for a total of 61 remaining parking spaces. Per the NMC Section 17.03.040
(Required Number of Spaces and Parking Matrix), a minimum of one (1) parking space is required
for every 250 square feet of gross floor area. Based on the existing restaurant building on site, 22
parking spaces are required. The subject property will remain compliant with parking requirements.
Location Proposed and Alternative Locations Considered
The Wireless Telecommunications Facilities Ordinance in the NMC Section 17.04.270 indicates that
wireless telecommunications facilities are encouraged to be located on existing buildings and
structures and in the following order of preference:
1. Collocation with existing facilities located in non-residential zones.
2. Manufacturing zones.
3. Commercial zones.
4. Other nonresidential zones, except open space zones.
5. On existing signal, power, light or similar kinds of poles in nonresidential zones.
6. Public property (i.e., city facilities) not in residential zones.
7. Public and private installations on water tanks, existing communication towers and other similar
  uses.
8. Public rights-of-way adjacent to manufacturing and commercial zones.
9. Parks and community facilities (i.e., places of worship, community centers) in residential zones
  or areas.
The project site is located within the C-3 (General Commercial) zone and is currently developed
with commercial use. The Applicant identified the placement of the facility in the rear of the property
as the least intrusive location to minimize visual impacts along major arterial streets. In addition, the
Applicant has also identified five (5) alternative off-site locations where a freestanding tower might
be feasible to close service gaps. The Applicant noted that out of the five properties, the subject
property was deemed the most feasible and least intrusive candidate with landlord interest.
Noise
The Noise Ordinance in the NMC Section 9.04.120.B identifies the assumed ambient noise levels
on variously zoned properties in the City and states that an average noise level reading that exceeds
the ambient noise level at the property line of any property by more than five (5) decibels shall be
 Norwalk Planning Commission  January 14, 2026
Wireless Telecommunications Permit No. 2024-02  Page No. 5
Director Approval Request No. 2025-09

deemed to be prima facie evidence of a violation. The presumed ambient noise level in commercial
zones is 60 A-weighted decibels (dbA) at any time. An acoustical analysis report for the Proposed
Project has been prepared (see Attachment F). The report concluded that based on the project
information available, calculations show that, with the proposed eight (8) foot high CMU enclosure
around the equipment constructed to the standards detailed in the proposed plans, noise impacts
from the proposed equipment are not expected to exceed the City’s noise limits. The report also
noted no mitigation is deemed necessary.
Propagation Maps
As part of the Applicant’s submittal, a propagation map illustrating the existing coverage limitations
within the target service area is provided (see Attachment G). Currently, users within this area
experience poor or no signal strength, resulting in dropped calls, slow data speeds, and unreliable
connectivity. The current gap in the area is highlighted in yellow, which signify weak service in the
“Current Coverage Map”.
The proposed wireless telecommunications facility will fill this gap by providing targeted signal
coverage within the deficient zone. The installation of the Proposed Project will enhance signal
strength throughout the previously underserved area, transitioning those zones to green, which
indicate optimal service levels in the “Coverage with Orr Map”. The proposed facility aligns with
surrounding network infrastructure while accounting for local terrain, existing structures, and user
density.
Maintenance
The proposed wireless telecommunications facility is unmanned and will be operated by Verizon for
twenty-four hours a day, seven (7) days per week. Verizon’s Network Operations Center (NOC)
continuously monitors its facilities through their remote network monitoring. Monitoring includes
equipment performance and alarms, outage detection and diagnostics, and remote trouble shooting
and control. Routine maintenance includes, but is not limited to, testing the backup power, monthly
testing on the generator, and monthly field assurance manager visits. The project site’s landscaping,
trash, and graffiti will be maintained by the property owner.
Applicant Community Outreach
On October 30, 2025, the Applicant hosted a community outreach meeting due to the subject site’s
proximity to residential properties. Notice of this meeting was mailed by the Applicant to property
owners within 500 feet of the property. One property owner attended the meeting and voiced
concerns regarding the proximity of the facility to residential property. The Applicant provided a
presentation on the Proposed Project and information on the Planning Commission hearing.

 compatibility with the community to the maximum extent reasonably feasible.

economically feasible and where co-location would not harm community compatibility.

allow for future co-location.

The proposed project, the Verizon telecommunications facility to be known as “ORR” (Project ID 17122262),
consists of the construction of an unmanned telecommunications facility to include equipment cabinets and a
30 kW backup generator within an eight-foot-high CMU enclosure. The project site is located at 12616 Pioneer

The purpose of this report is to assess noise impacts from the equipment at the Verizon facility and to determine
if mitigation is necessary and feasible to reduce project-related property line noise impacts to comply with
applicable noise limits. Noise limits specified within the City of Norwalk Code of Ordinances must be met at
surrounding noise-sensitive receivers.

2.0  Introduction
This acoustical analysis report is submitted to satisfy the noise requirements of the City of Norwalk. Its purpose
is to assess noise impacts from on-site project-related mechanical noise sources and to determine if mitigation
will be necessary to reduce the noise impacts to meet the applicable noise limits of the City of Norwalk.

All noise level or sound level values presented herein are expressed in terms of decibels (dB), with A-weighting,
abbreviated “dBA,” to approximate the hearing sensitivity of humans. Time-averaged noise levels are expressed
by the symbol LEQ for a specified duration. Unless a different time period is specified, LEQ is implied to mean
a period of one hour. These metrics are used to express noise levels for both measurement and municipal
regulations, for land use guidelines, and for enforcement of noise ordinances.

Some of the data may also be presented as octave-band-filtered and/or 1/3-octave-band-filtered data, which
are a series of sound spectra centered about each stated frequency, with half of the bandwidth above and half
of the bandwidth below each stated frequency. This data is typically used for machinery noise analysis and
barrier calculations. Sound pressure is the actual noise experienced by a human or registered by a sound level
instrument. When sound pressure is used to describe a noise source, the distance from the noise source must
be specified in order to provide complete information.

4.0  Methodology and Equipment
4.1  Methodology

Modeling of the outdoor noise environment is accomplished using CadnaA Version 2024 MR 1, which is a
model-based computer program developed by DataKustik for predicting noise impacts in a wide variety of
conditions. CadnaA (Computer Aided Noise Abatement) assists in the calculation, presentation, assessment,
and alleviation of noise exposure. It allows for the input of project information such as noise source data,
barriers, structures, and topography to create a detailed model and uses the most up-to-date calculation
standards to predict outdoor noise impacts. Noise standards used by CadnaA that are particularly relevant to
this analysis include ISO 9613-2 (Attenuation of sound during propagation outdoors). CadnaA provides results
that are in line with basic acoustical calculations for distance attenuation and barrier insertion loss.

Chapter 9.04. OFFENSES AGAINST PUBLIC PEACE AND
DECENCY
Article III. Noise
§ 9.04.100. Noise prohibited.

No person shall make, continue or cause to be made or continued, any loud, unnecessary or unusual
noise, or any noise which either annoys, disturbs, injures or endangers the comfort, repose, health,
peace or safety of others within the limits of the City.
(Prior code § 5-17.1; Ord. 21-1722 § 2)

§ 9.04.110. General definitions.

As used in this article:

"A band level" means the total sound level of all noise as measured with a sound-level meter using the A
weighting network. The unit is dbA.

"Day" means the time period from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.

"Decibel (db)" means a unit of level which denotes the ratio between two quantities which are
proportional to power; the number of decibels corresponding to the ratio to two amounts of power is 10
times the logarithm to the base 10 of this ratio.

"Emergency work" means work made necessary to restore property to a safe condition following a
public calamity, work required to protect persons or property from an imminent exposure to danger, or
work by private or public utility service.

"Night" means the time period from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.

"Noise level in decibels" means the A-weighted sound pressure level as measured using the slow
dynamic characteristic for sound level meters specified in ASA S1 4-1961, American Standard
Specification for General Purpose Sound Level Meters, or latest revision. The reference pressure is 20
micronewtons/square meter (2 x 10-4 microbar).

"Person" means a person, firm, association, copartnership, joint venture, corporation or any entity,
public or private in nature.

"Sound level meter" means an instrument including a microphone, an amplifier, an output meter and
frequency weighting networks for the measurement of noise and sound levels in a specified manner as
specified in ASA S1 4-1961, American Standard Specification for General Purpose Sound Level Meters,
or latest revision.
 (Prior code § 5-17.2; Ord. 21-1722 § 2)

§ 9.04.120. Ambient noise level.

A.  "Ambient noise" means the all-encompassing noise associated with a given environment being
  usually a composite of sounds with many sources near and far, without inclusion of intruding noises
  from isolated identifiable sources.

B.  Unless sound-level meter readings determine the ambient noise level in a given environment to be
  higher, the ambient noise levels in Norwalk are presumed to be as follows:

  Decibels  Time  Zone
  45 dbA  Night  Residential
  55 dbA  Day  Residential
  60 dbA  Anytime  Commercial
  65 dbA  Anytime  All other zones
(Prior code § 5-17.3; Ord. 21-1722 § 2)

§ 9.04.130. Decibel measurement criteria.

A.  Any decibel measurement made pursuant to provisions of article shall be based on a reference
  sound pressure of 0.0002 microbars as measured in any octave band with center frequency, in
  cycles per second, as follows: 63, 125, 250, 500,1000, 2000, 4000 and 8000 or as measured with a
  sound-level meter using the A weighting network, and using the slow meter response.

B.  Measurements shall be taken with the microphone located at any point on the property line, but no
  closer than three feet from any wall and not less than three feet above the ground.

C.  A minimum of three readings shall be taken at two minute intervals. The sound level shall be the
  average of these readings.
(Prior code § 5-17.4; Ord. 21-1722 § 2)

§ 9.04.140. General noise regulations.

A.  Use Restricted. Notwithstanding any other provision of this article and in addition to this article, it is
  unlawful for any person to wilfully make or continue, or cause to be made or continued, any loud,
  unnecessary or unusual noise which disturbs the peace or quiet of any neighborhood or which
  causes discomfort or annoyance to any reasonable person of normal sensitiveness residing in the
  area.

B.  Prima Facie Violation. An average noise level reading measured pursuant to Section 9.04.130
  which exceeds the ambient noise level at the property line of any residential land (or if a
  condominium or apartment house, within any adjoining apartment) by more than five decibels shall
  be deemed to be prima fade evidence of a violation of the provisions of this article.
(Prior code § 5-17.5; Ord. 21-1722 § 2)

Article V. Discretionary Approvals and Permits
§ 17.02.210. Conditional use permits.

A.  Authority of Planning Commission to Grant Conditional Use Permits. The Planning Commission
  may grant a conditional use permit for those uses which are so allowed by this title. In the granting
  of any conditional use permit, the Planning Commission may impose such conditions as it
  determines are necessary and reasonable to protect the best interests of the surrounding property
  or neighborhood and to ensure compliance with the general purpose and intent of this title and the
  general plan, and shall impose such conditions as are required by the provisions of this title.

B.  Purpose of and Required Showing for Conditional Use Permit. The purpose of a conditional use
  permit shall be to ensure that the degree of compatibility required by this title shall be maintained
  with respect to the particular use on the particular site, giving consideration to other existing and
  potential uses within the general area in which such use is located or proposed to be located.

C.  Notice and Hearing on Application for Conditional Use Permit. Upon the filing by the property
  owners, by a lessee having a written and acknowledged lease, or by a beneficial or equitable owner
  of an application for a conditional use permit, in accordance with the procedures and requirements
  set forth in Chapter 17.02, Article II, which application sets forth fully the grounds for, and the facts
  claimed to justify the granting of, a conditional use permit, the Planning Commission shall give
  public notice, as provided in this title, of the intention to consider at a public hearing the granting of
  a conditional use permit, and shall hold at least one public hearing thereon.

D.  Planning Commission Report on Findings and Decision. No more than 40 calendar days following
  the closing of a public hearing on an application for a conditional use permit, the Planning
  Commission shall, unless it adopts a motion directing that another public hearing be held thereon,
  adopt its findings and final decision by formal report. The report shall recite, among other things, the
  facts and reasons which, in the Planning Commission's opinion, make the granting or denial of a
  conditional use permit necessary to carry out the provisions and general purpose of this title, and
  shall order that a conditional use permit is thereby granted or denied; and, if such report orders that
  the conditional use is granted, it shall also recite such conditions and limitations as are imposed.
  Failure of the Planning Commission to file its report within such period shall not constitute the
  granting or denial of a conditional use permit, and shall not affect the validity of a report issued after
  the expiration of such period.

E.  Report of the Planning Commission. The formal report of the Planning Commission, granting or
  denying any application for a conditional use permit, shall be promptly filed, shall be numbered
  consecutively in the order of its filing, and shall become a permanent record in the file of the
  Planning Commission.

  filing of a report granting or denying a conditional use permit, a copy of the report shall be delivered
  or mailed by certified or registered mail to the applicant or applicants, utilizing, in the case of

C.  Review of Application.

  1.  The Director of Community Development or the Director of Public Services/City Engineer may
  administratively review and approve an application for a wireless telecommunication facility
  permit if the facility complies with Article IV of Chapter 17.04 and as proposed is architecturally
  integrated with the existing development (i.e., building or structure) so as to be screened,
  camouflaged and visually nonobtrusive. Notwithstanding, the Director may at his or her
  discretion refer the wireless telecommunications facility permit to the Planning Commission for
  review.

  2.  The Planning Commission shall review applications not otherwise reviewed by the Director,
  including, but not limited to, applications in the public right-of-way or located in a residential
   zone.

D.  Peer Review.

  1.  The Director of Community Development or the Director of Public Services/City Engineer is
  authorized to retain on behalf of the City an independent technical expert to peer review any
  application for a wireless telecommunications facility permit. The review is intended to be a
  review of technical aspects of the proposed wireless telecommunications facility and shall
  address all of the following:

  a.  Compliance with applicable radio frequency emission standards;

  b.  Whether any requested exception is necessary to close a significant gap in coverage and
  is the least intrusive means of doing so;

  c.  The accuracy and completeness of submissions;

  d.  Technical demonstration of the unavailability of alternative sites or configurations and/or
  coverage analysis;

  e.  The applicability of analysis techniques and methodologies;

  f.  The validity of conclusions reached; and

  g.  Any specific technical issues designated by the City.

  The cost of this review shall be paid by the applicant through a deposit pursuant to an adopted
  fee schedule.

  2.  If a permittee proposes any modifications to any wireless telecommunications facility permit
  after said permit is granted, the permittee shall submit an application to the Planning
  Commission for consideration; provided, however, that the City and Planning Commission
  need not accept and/or process said application unless and until the permittee (a)
  demonstrates the existing wireless telecommunications facility's compliance with all applicable
  local requirements; and (b) certifies that the existing wireless telecommunications facility
  complies with all applicable State, and Federal requirements. In the case of collocations, minor
  structural modifications may be permitted if necessary to accommodate said co-located facility.

E.  Notice and Hearing on Application for Wireless Telecommunications Permit. Upon the filing by the
  property owners or its authorized agent (if the agent provides written authority to the City that it is
  authorized to file the application such as a letter of authorization), of an application which sets forth
  fully the grounds for, and the facts claimed to justify the granting of a wireless telecommunications
  permit, the Planning Commission shall give public notice, as provided in this title, of the intention to
  consider at a public hearing the granting of such permit, and shall hold at least one public hearing
  thereon. In the case of an application reviewed by the Director, no public notice or hearing is
  required.

F.  Report on Findings and Decision. Following the closing of a public hearing, if applicable, on an
  application for a wireless telecommunications permit, the Planning Commission shall, unless it
  adopts a motion directing that another public hearing be held thereon, adopt its findings by
  resolution. If the application is denied, the Planning Commission shall adopt a Resolution setting
  forth the findings for such denial based on substantial evidence contained in the administrative
  record. In the case of an application reviewed by the Director, the Director shall adopt its findings by
  report. The resolution or report shall recite, among other things, the facts and reasons which, in the
  Planning Commission or Director's opinion, make the granting or denial of a wireless
  telecommunications permit necessary to carry out the provisions and general purpose of this
  section and Article IV of Chapter 17.04, and shall order that a wireless telecommunications permit
  is thereby granted or denied; and, if such resolution or report orders that the permit be granted, it
  shall also recite such conditions and limitations as are imposed.
 G. Resolution or Report. The resolution of the Planning Commission, or in the case of an application
  reviewed by the Director of Community Development, the report of the Director of Community
  Development, granting or denying any application for a wireless telecommunications permit, shall
  be promptly filed, shall be numbered consecutively in the order of its filing, and shall become a
  permanent record in the file of the Community Development Department.

H.  Notice of Decision. Not later than three calendar days following the filing of a resolution or report
  granting or denying a wireless telecommunications permit, a copy of the resolution or report shall
  be delivered or mailed by certified or registered mail to the applicant or applicants, utilizing, in the
  case of mailing, any address shown on the application or other documents filed with the Community
  Development Department. Notice of the action granting or denying a wireless telecommunications
  permit shall be delivered or mailed to each member of the City Council, the City Manager, the City
  Attorney, and each person who has filed with the department a request for notice of decision in the
  particular case. A copy of such report shall be posted in a prominent place in the City Hall,
  designated for such purpose by the City Manager, from not later than, three days following until at
  least the 10th day following the filing of the resolution or report, but failure to so post any such
  notice shall not extend the time of becoming effective of any decision of the Commission or
  Director.

I.  Decision When Final—Appeal. The decision of the Planning Commission or Director shall become
  final and effective 10 calendar days after delivery or mailing of all of the notices required by Section
  17.02.295(E) unless prior to 5:00 p.m. of the 10th day, either of the following has occurred:

  1.  A written appeal has been filed with the City Clerk by an applicant or by a person specially
  aggrieved; or

  2.  The City Council elects to review the decision of the Commission.

J.  Appeals Procedure.

  1.  If an appeal in writing is filed with the City Clerk as provided in Section 17.02.295(F)(1) or if the
  City Council elects on its own motion to review the action of the Planning Commission as
  provided in Section 17.02.295(F)(2), the complete record of the case shall be transmitted to the
  City Council. In the case of a decision by the Director of Community Development, the
  complete record of the case shall be transmitted to the Planning Commission.

  2.  The City Council shall hold one public hearing notice of which shall be given in the manner
  prescribed by Sections 17.02.050 and 17.02.060, within 40 days of the filing of a written appeal
  or the adoption by the Council of a motion to review the action of the Commission. In the case
  of an appeal to the Planning Commission, the Planning Commission shall hold one public
  hearing notice of which shall be given in the manner prescribed by Sections 17.02.050 and
  17.02.060, within 40 days of the filing of a written appeal.

  3.  The reviewing body shall announce, within 40 days of the closing of the public hearing, its
  decision granting or denying a wireless telecommunications permit by adoption of a resolution,
  which shall set forth the reasons for its decision and shall indicate wherein such decision
  conforms to the intent and purpose of this section and Article IV of Chapter 17.04. In such
  proceedings, no finding, decision, order, stipulation or other action of the Commission shall
  bind the City Council.

  4.  The action of the City Council shall be final. The action of the Planning Commission may be
  appealed to the City Council pursuant to the provisions of this section.

  5.  Within 10 calendar days following the adoption of the resolution, one copy thereof shall be
  forwarded to the applicant or the appellant or both, as the case may be, and one copy shall be
  transmitted to the Commission for filing.

K.  Time Interval for Re-application for a Wireless Telecommunications Facility Permit. No permit
  application which has been denied in whole or in part shall be filed again within six months from the
  date of such denial except upon proof of changed conditions or by permission of the Director.
 L.  Expiration. Any wireless telecommunications permit shall be null and void:

  1.  If not exercised within the time specified in such wireless telecommunications permit or, if no
  date is specified, within one year from the date of approval of the wireless telecommunications
  permit;

  2.  Upon revocation as provided herein.

M. Revocation. The Planning Commission may, after a hearing, compliance being had with applicable
  requirements of Chapter 17.02, Article I, revoke, modify or suspend any wireless
  telecommunications permit on any one or more of the following grounds:

  1.  That the wireless telecommunications permit was obtained by fraud or misrepresentation;

  2.  That the wireless telecommunications permit granted is being, or within the recent past has
  been, exercised contrary to the terms or conditions of such approval or in violation of any
  statute, ordinance, law or regulation; or

  3.  That the use permitted by the wireless telecommunications permit is being, or within the recent
  past has been, exercised so as to be detrimental to the public health or safety or as to
  constitute a nuisance.

  4.  Failure to comply with any condition of approval or the standards in Article IV of Chapter 17.04.
  In the event of termination pursuant to this section, the permittee shall remove its wireless
  telecommunications facility at its own expense and shall repair and restore all property affected
  by the placement, maintenance, and removal of the wireless telecommunications facility to a
  condition satisfactory to the Director.

N.  Findings. A wireless telecommunications facility permit may be granted only if the following findings
  are made by the reviewing authority.

  1.  The proposed wireless telecommunications facility has been designed to achieve compatibility
  with the community to the maximum extent reasonably feasible;

  2.  An alternative configuration will not increase community compatibility or is not reasonably
  feasible;

  3.  Alternative locations on the site will not increase community compatibility or are not reasonably
  feasible;

  4.  The location of the wireless telecommunications facility on alternative sites will not increase
  community compatibility or is not reasonably feasible;

  5.  The proposed facility is necessary to close a significant gap in coverage and is the least
  intrusive means of doing so;

  6.  The applicant has submitted a statement of its willingness to allow other carriers to collocate
  on the proposed wireless telecommunications facility wherever technically and economically
  feasible and where co-location would not harm community compatibility;

  7.  Noise generated by equipment will not be excessive, annoying nor be detrimental to the public
  health, safety, and welfare; and

  8.  In the case of a wireless telecommunications facility in the public right-of-way, the applicant is a
  telephone corporation and has been issued a certificate of public convenience and necessity
  issued by the California Public Utilities Commission, which expressly states the applicant's
  authority to provide the telecommunications service the applicant proposes to provide through
  the wireless telecommunications facility, which is the subject of the application.
